name: Queued-task runner
description: A queued task runs once, under the persona it names, and always comes back with a reported result, including after a restart.
purpose: Takes a person's queued requests to a reported outcome, so they run on time without anyone having to start them by hand.
approach: Claims each due task once, runs it, and reports the result back to its queue.
out_of_scope: Deciding what a queued task should say or do.
milestones: 1. Every lifecycle case passes on the lane's poller and executor: done, failed, needs-you, duplicate, lost claim, not-yet-due, team-scoped and unconfigured. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: Discovery is event driven with signature dedup across restarts and a backend-aware claim as a second guard. A persona activates only when asked for, never from a bare mention of a name. Folder sync keeps human text and pushes each bullet once. Cancelled tasks need no patch because the backend already set the status.
measures_of_success: Poll, claim, run and report behave correctly across done, failed, needs-you, duplicate, lost-claim, not-yet-due, team-scoped and unconfigured cases, with persona choice, folder sync and scheduling correct. Standing conditions: Claim each due task once. Run it as the right persona against its work folder. Report an outcome for every task. Run none early.
parameters: The poller takes a configuration with credentials, team, adapters and a concurrency bound; personas take a skills root, registry, assignment fields and flags for model-judged asks; the lane driver takes check, once or loop modes and an env file.
inputs: Queued tasks from the backend, the configuration, persona registry and folder map.
outputs: A reported status on each task (with result text or decision id), updated folder sync files, and logs.
effects: Claims tasks on the backend, writes the sync file in work folders, may post notes, and spawns deep runs.
usage_notes: Start a lane with the shared driver and pick one-shot mode for cron or loop mode for a service. Use structured assignment for personas where tasks name an owner.

name: Critical Thinking
description: Holds every request the system serves (a chat turn, a queued task, a deep run) to the specification's relevant metric by code: it finds the slice, has the metric read before and after, and answers a regression or a missing metric instead of only displaying it, so the specification is applied everywhere rather than where the work is largest.
purpose: Makes sure everything the system does applies the relevant ESOI metric and leaves it improved, or at least not worse.
approach: Finds the relevant slice of the specification for each request, measures its authoritative metric before and after by code, and holds the result to improve or not regress, proposing a metric where none exists.
out_of_scope: Finding the slice and reading a metric (the specification slice, meters and ledger do that), writing a run's changes back onto the records, and choosing which metric a solution should have, which is the owner's to confirm.
milestones: 1. A replayed set of requests across chat turns, queued tasks and deep runs exists, each labelled with the metric it should be held to or none, and deep_runs_only and instruction_only have recorded results on it. 2. every_request_measured holds every request whose labelled metric can be read, with no time added before the reply. 3. measured_proposed_and_answered leaves no regression and no missing metric without a response, and proposes a metric for the metric-less requests.
knowledge: The specification owner's definition (2026-10-28): an enforcer of the effective application of ESOI on every request, making sure the relevant metrics are applied and improving on everything the system does; a person's quest metrics and experiments are one case of it, not its definition. The owner's standing principle: a rule for AI is built into the flow and enforced by code, never left to an instruction. Built and settled 2026-10-22, by direction rather than a measured win: around every deep goal the slice is found without a model (core/spec_slice.py), the metric is read before and after by the runner's own meters (core/metric_meter.py), rows go to a ledger and are reconciled (core/metric_results.py), and a changed run with nothing on record is asked once and otherwise marked missing (core/goal_metrics.py); the rows are shown in the terminal and the host's chat. Missing, read in the code on 2026-10-28: the goal metrics are created only in the deep run (core/orchestrator_deep_run.py), so chat turns and in-process work take no reading; a slice exists only when a repository's records are found and the selection is confident, and a quest's own specification reaches chat through the intent frame, not a slice; when the reading after is worse, nothing acts; a missing metric is shown and not followed up. Open recommendation, not decided: keep this as the enforcing role that uses iterate-by-spec and the metric modules as mechanisms, rather than widening iterate-by-spec, because its unit is every request and its best is coverage and no regression, while iterate-by-spec is defined per deep goal and judged by first-pass acceptance; if its only arm turns out to be iterate-by-spec applied everywhere, the two should merge.
measures_of_success: Every request whose metric can be read is measured before and after by code; none is left worse without a response; a request with no metric gets one proposed; for a person's quest, an uncertain choice leads to a proposed experiment. Standing conditions: Decide from the ledger and the runner's own records, never from a model's words. Never invent a reading. Add no time before a chat reply.
parameters: Which kinds of request are held (chat, task, deep), which meter reads a chat turn and when, what counts as a regression, the response to one (retry, revert, follow-up, escalation), and whether a metric is proposed when none applies.
inputs: The request, its slice of the specification or the quest's own specification, the ledger and the runner's records of what changed.
outputs: Per request: the metric applied with its reading before and after, or the reason none applies, or a proposed metric; and for a regression or a missing metric, the response taken.
effects: Reads metrics through the meters, after a chat reply in the background; writes ledger rows; may open a follow-up task or a proposal; never edits the owner's records without consent.
usage_notes: Selected today: deep_runs_only. instruction_only is the floor that shows what code enforcement adds.

name: Multi-source evidence retriever
description: Reads from every source a person's work already lives in (local files, databases, workspace documents and chat, MCP servers and hosted backends) through one stack, so a broken source reports an error while the others still answer.
purpose: Gives a planner the material it needs to ground a decision or answer, drawn from the sources a person's work already lives in.
approach: Reads the material each question needs from every configured source, and reports a source that fails without stopping the others.
out_of_scope: Writing to any source, searching the open web for material no configured source holds, and reading past the roots and allowlists a person configured.
milestones: 1. The composite stack finds the right document in the top three answers across the handbook questions, each answer is readable, and a broken source returns an error while the others still answer.
knowledge: Per-source adapters are complementary sources, not alternatives, so a composite stack is the unit that is ranked. Some sources do not search: a drive has no search so its policy is to list and read, a notion source locates by row, and an MCP result measures plumbing because the server does the search. Fixtures are written rather than recorded and keyword gathering misses paraphrases. A remote search must be scoped because a composite broadcasts unscoped requests.
measures_of_success: The right document is found near the top for questions over a representative corpus, the answer is readable, and a broken source returns an error observation while the other sources still answer.
parameters: Per source: the root or base address, an alias for namespacing, token provider or credential source, allowlists of tools or databases, cache lifetime, size and time budgets. At composition level: the ordered list of member adapters.
inputs: A read request (path with optional line range or heading), a regular-expression search with an optional scope, or a structured query specification; plus discovery calls to list and describe sources and operations.
outputs: Observation values carrying text, a path or source label, and a kind, with error observations in place of exceptions.
effects: Read-only network and file access, in-memory caching, and wall-clock spent on requests. No writes to any source.
usage_notes: Wire members into the composite and let the planner use discovery before reading. Always scope remote searches and keep credentials injected, never embedded. Treat every adapter as never raising.
